subject: maths
question: Train P going at a speed of 72 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 393 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks at 42 km/hr, in 1.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will train P take to completely cross train R of length 468 m, going at 63 km/hr in the opposite direction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Same direction: Relative speed = 72 − 42 = 30 km/hr = 25/3 m/s

Time = 1.5 min = 90 sec ⇒ Total length (P + Q) = 90 × 25/3 = 750 m

⇒ Length of P = 750 − 393 = 357 m

Opposite direction: Relative speed = 72 + 63 = 135 km/hr = 37.5 m/s

**∴ Answer = 22 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of P = 72 km/hr, Q = 42 km/hr, length of Q = 393 m, time = 1.5 min

Length of R = 468 m, speed of R = 63 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Convert speeds into m/s

⇒ Relative speed (same direction) = 72 − 42 = 30 km/hr = 30 × 5/18 = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Time = 1.5 min = 90 sec

⇒ Total length (P + Q) = Speed × Time = (25/3) × 90 = 750 m

⇒ Length of train P = 750 − 393 = 357 m

⇒ Relative speed (opposite direction) = 72 + 63 = 135 km/hr = 135 × 5/18 = 37.5 m/s

⇒ Total distance = 357 + 468 = 825 m

⇒ Time = 825 ÷ 37.5

⇒ = 22 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 22 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Same direction ⇒ difference, Opposite direction ⇒ sum

Train Crossing

Total distance = sum of lengths of both trains

Unit Conversion

km/hr to m/s = × 5/18

Key Strategy

First find unknown train length, then apply second condition
